venues.name: Gothic Theatre

seatingFormat.note: Official venue page: general admission/standing unless an event says otherwise, with very limited first-come balcony seating. Wikipedia describes a seated section plus standing-room section.

agePolicy.text: Shows are 16+ unless listed otherwise; individual shows can be all ages, 18+ or 21+. Under-16s need a parent/guardian (ages 0-10) or a ticketed adult (11-15) at 16+ shows, and are not admitted to 18+/21+ shows. Valid ID required.

doors.text: Per-event door times are not given on the venue page; box office opens 1 hour before doors and guests are advised to arrive before or around posted doors. Quick Pass lets you enter first when doors open to the public, but it is not early entry.

parking.summary: Venue page says parking is street parking (watch for residential permit restrictions) plus pay lots around the neighborhood. No on-site lot or prices sourced. Tripadvisor reviewers mention limited parking, a nearby pay lot, and walking a few blocks.

transit.summary: Venue lists RTD light rail with roughly a 15-20 minute walk from Englewood Station, and bus routes 0, 12, 27, 35 and ART.

policies.bag: Large backpacks, suitcases, beach bags and equipment bags are prohibited. Walk-through metal detectors are used at all events; no outside food or drink, no weapons.
policies.other: Concessions are cashless; box office takes cash and card ($2.50 per-ticket box office fee). Tickets mostly via AXS Mobile app. Camera policy varies by show.

accessibility.summary: No special accessible ticket needed; tell event security on arrival and staff bring a chair and escort you to the ADA section. Service animals allowed, pets not. Website accessibility help line (888) 226-0076 (not ticketing).

area.summary: Located at 3263 S Broadway in Englewood, a South Broadway corridor setting; opened 1925 as a cinema and operated by AEG Live. Nearby food/late-night details not verified.

sound.summary: No sound-quality comments found in sources reviewed. Reviewers on Tripadvisor generally describe good views and closeness to the stage.

whyPeopleLikeIt.text: Small, historic theatre where reviewers say you can get close to performers and see well from most spots.
Both a standing floor and some elevated seating exist, so you can choose your spot.

considerBeforeAttending.text: Balcony seating is very limited and first-come; a reviewer reports single-row barstool seating so others behind must stand.
Allow extra time for metal-detector screening at the door.
Age rule varies by show (default 16+); check the listing and bring ID.
Reviewers report limited parking and mixed experiences with door staff and some rowdy patrons; anecdotal.

venues.notes: Capacity unverified: Wikipedia infobox says 1,100 but text says just under 1,000, and the venue page gives none. Re-entry not stated. Community evidence is a handful of Tripadvisor reviews only.

venues.name: Bluebird Theater

seatingFormat.note: Official FAQ: general admission/standing unless listed otherwise, with a very limited number of first-come balcony seats. Wikipedia describes a tiered layout with a balcony overlooking the room.

agePolicy.text: Shows are 16+ unless noted; individual shows can be all ages, 18+ or 21+. Under-16s need a parent/guardian (0-10) or ticketed adult (11-15) at 16+ shows; 16-17 not admitted to 18+; 18-20 not admitted to 21+.

doors.text: No standard door time on the FAQ; box office opens 30 minutes before doors and guests are advised to arrive before or around posted doors. Quick Pass gives first entry at doors, not early entry.

parking.summary: Venue says to use the lot across the street (Paradise Cleaners lot); if full, street parking on Colfax, 16th St and 14th St. Avoid Adams and Cook streets (permit-only residential). Tripadvisor reviewers call parking difficult/limited on Colfax and say the lot fills fast.

transit.summary: Venue lists RTD bus routes 15, 20, 32 and 40.

policies.bag: Large backpacks, suitcases, beach bags and equipment bags are prohibited. Walk-through metal detectors at all events; no outside food or drink.
policies.other: Concessions cashless; box office accepts cash and card ($2.50 per-ticket box office fee). Camera policy varies by show. Valid ID accepted forms listed on FAQ.

accessibility.summary: No special accessible ticket needed; tell event security on arrival and staff bring a chair and escort you to the ADA section. Service animals allowed, pets not. A reviewer who needed accessible seating was given folding chairs at the front side (community-reported).

area.summary: At 3317 E Colfax Ave near City Park; operated by AEG Live; historic 1914 theater. Specific nearby food/late-night notes not verified.

sound.summary: Reviewers describe a terraced floor giving good views from nearly anywhere, an intimate small room, and one praised the acoustics. Based on few reviews.

whyPeopleLikeIt.text: Small, intimate room with tiered floor so sightlines are reportedly good.
Historic building (opened 1914, National Register listed) reopened as a music venue in 1994.

considerBeforeAttending.text: Parking is tight on Colfax; the lot across the street fills quickly, so arrive early or use transit.
Do not park on Adams or Cook streets (permit-only).
Balcony seats are very few and first-come; most shows are standing.
Age rule varies by show (default 16+); bring valid ID. Concessions are cashless.

venues.notes: Capacity from Wikipedia only (550); venue pages do not state it. Re-entry not stated. Community evidence is few Tripadvisor reviews.

venues.name: Summit Music Hall

seatingFormat.note: General admission, mostly standing floor with a balcony; a smaller Moon Room is in the same building. Ticket Fairy lists capacity approximations and says occupancy depends on setup.

agePolicy.text: Varies by event; shows with no stated restriction are all ages, others 18+ or 21+. The event listing controls; bring valid photo ID for age-restricted shows and alcohol.

doors.text: No set door time stated; box office opens 1 hour before doors on show days.

parking.summary: No on-site lot. Paid lots and garages around LoDo (e.g., SP+ at 1615 18th St, garage at 1757 Market St per a Ticketmaster blog). Street meters have 2-hour limits. Prices rise on Rockies game nights; no fixed event rate published.

transit.summary: Union Station (rail and bus) is about a 10-minute walk; RTD stops listed near 18th and Blake and 20th and Blake.

policies.bag: Ticketmaster blog (2020s, possibly dated) says clear bag policy, max 12x6x12 in, small clutches allowed; confirm with the venue.
policies.reentry: No re-entry per Ticket Fairy venue page.
policies.other: Venue-operated purchases are cashless. Pizza by the slice on site.

accessibility.summary: Designated ADA area to the right of the stage (per Ticket Fairy); no elevator to the balcony. Ticketmaster blog advises ADA guests to arrive just before doors. A recycled-records guide describes an ADA section stage left with ramp access.

area.summary: Located at 1902 Blake St in LoDo near Coors Field and Union Station. Nearby bars skew to a sports crowd and Dairy Block has coffee and food, per Ticketmaster blog.

sound.summary: Venue-side page cites a Outline GTO C-12 line-source system. A local record-store guide says fans and bands praise the modern line-array; pit gives close views and the three-sided balcony gives elevated views.

whyPeopleLikeIt.text: Mid-size room with a standing pit plus balcony on three sides, so you can choose close or elevated views.
Walkable from Union Station, so transit is a practical alternative to driving.

considerBeforeAttending.text: No re-entry, so plan to leave only once.
Balcony has no elevator.
Parking costs rise on Rockies game nights and meters cap at two hours.
Age rule varies per event; bring valid ID. Venue purchases are cashless.

venues.notes: Capacity commonly cited ~1,100 (Ticketmaster blog, Ticket Fairy); Ticket Fairy lists other figures (up to 1,350 fire-code) and one guide says 900-1,100, so treat as approximate. Ticket Fairy and the recycled-records guide are third-party; Live Nation venue page could not be read. Bag policy source may be dated.

venues.name: Marquis Theater

seatingFormat.note: General admission, mostly standing; limited bar stools/tables first-come (Ticketmaster blog, dated 2020/2022).

agePolicy.text: Listed on each event page; if none is listed the show is all ages. Guests 3 and up need a ticket. Valid photo ID needed for age-restricted shows and alcohol.

doors.text: No standard door time stated; box office opens 1 hour before doors on show days (and noon-5pm Fridays). Will Call opens one hour before doors.

parking.summary: Venue is surrounded by paid street and off-street parking, including a paid lot just south; Marquis does not run these lots and partners with ParkWhiz for pre-booking. Ticketmaster blog also mentions metered Larimer St and lots nearby. No prices sourced.

policies.bag: Backpacks and large bags prohibited and visitors may be searched (Ticketmaster blog, dated); flash photography, outside food/drink and weapons also prohibited.
policies.other: Venue is cashless at all points of sale except the box office; cash can be converted to a prepaid card. Tickets are non-transferable; bring ID and the purchase card to Will Call. Lost items: email marquis@livenation.com.

accessibility.summary: Ticketmaster blog advises guests needing ADA seating to arrive just before doors to be seated. No further detail verified.

area.summary: At 2009 Larimer St in LoDo, about two blocks from Coors Field. On-site Marquis Pizza counter; nearby dining includes Mercantile and Terminal Bar (dated blog).

sound.summary: Wanderlog reviewers split on loudness (one says very loud, another says excellent for size) and praise sightlines in a small room; earplugs reportedly provided. A 2015 remodel added new sound and lighting per Ticketmaster blog.

whyPeopleLikeIt.text: Small room where reviewers say sightlines are good and you are close to the performers.
Reviewers like the bar and on-site pizza.

considerBeforeAttending.text: Venue is cashless except the box office.
Tickets are non-transferable; Will Call needs photo ID plus the purchasing card.
Parking is paid and not run by the venue; pre-book via ParkWhiz or expect paid lots.
Can be very loud; bring ear protection, especially for kids.

venues.notes: Capacity, seating and bag details come from a 2020 Ticketmaster blog (updated 2022) and may be dated. Transit, re-entry not verified. Colour from a single aggregator.

venues.name: Paramount Theatre

seatingFormat.note: Ticketed seating with orchestra (main level), mezzanine and balcony; Rate Your Seats also lists club, boxes and tables. Some events may use a different setup (not verified).

agePolicy.text: Varies by event; check each event's Ticketmaster page. For most shows, anyone 2 and older needs a ticket.

doors.text: No specific door time listed; staff recommend arriving when doors open to avoid security delays.

parking.summary: Tremont Garage (400 15th St) is free for most ticketed events: opens 2 hours before showtime, closes 60 minutes after; show digital ticket barcode at exit. Accessible spaces there. Rates for non-complimentary events not stated.

transit.summary: Light rail, bus and the free 16th Street Mall shuttle serve the theatre; check RTD for schedules.

policies.bag: Purses, cinch and sling bags up to 10x6x4 in allowed; medical/diaper bags up to 14x14x6 in; backpacks and oversized bags not allowed; no bag check. Handheld metal-detector screening.
policies.other: Tickets are digital (add to mobile wallet). Alcohol limited to two drinks per guest per ID check; alcohol cannot leave the venue (ejection and $250 citation). No smoking or vaping. Page appears dated, so confirm.

accessibility.summary: Accessible seating is main level only (mezzanine and balcony are stairs only). Use far-left door of main entrance at 1621 Glenarm Pl; drop-off in front. Elevator has limited capacity; only accessible restroom is in the main lobby. Free assistive listening devices with ID as collateral. Sign language/captioning needs 2 weeks notice via feedback@paramountdenver.com. Service dogs permitted.

area.summary: Downtown at 1621 Glenarm Pl, steps from the 16th Street Mall and Denver Pavilions with restaurants and bars nearby. Opened 1930, Art Deco movie palace.

sound.summary: No consistent sound or sightline commentary verified from sources reviewed.

whyPeopleLikeIt.text: Historic 1930 movie palace (National Register listed) with ornate interior and a Wurlitzer organ.
Free event parking in Tremont Garage for most ticketed shows plus downtown transit access.

considerBeforeAttending.text: No re-entry; leaving to smoke means you cannot return.
Bag rules are strict (small bags only, no backpacks, no bag check).
Mezzanine and balcony are stairs only; accessible seating is main level only.
Two-drink limit per ID check; digital tickets only.

venues.notes: Capacity from Wikipedia (1,870, 'seats'). FAQ page looks dated (references 2022 masks). Community sound/sightline and parking-difficulty colour not gathered; parking 'easy' is inferred from the venue's free-garage statement, not community reports.
